paper.title: Quantum Algorithm for Online Convex Optimization

settings.name_in_paper: Online convex optimization with quantum zeroth-order oracles (general convex losses)
unmapped: Feedback is a quantum zeroth-order oracle Q_{f_t} that can be queried in superposition, O(1) (4) queries per round after committing x_t
Completely adaptive adversary: f_t chosen after observing x_t
Player knows the convex set K, D and G
settings.definition_quote: A quantum zeroth-order oracle $Q_f$ is a unitary transformation that maps a quantum state $\ket{x}\ket{q}$ to the state $\ket{x}\ket{q+ f(x)}$ ... the adversary in our setting is \textit{completely adaptive}, who can choose $f_t$ after observing the player's choice $x_t$. ... The loss functions are G-Lipschitz continuous ... the feasible set $\mathcal{K}$ is bounded and its diameter has an upper bound $D$ ... $\mathcal{K},D,G$ are known to the player.

settings.name_in_paper: Online convex optimization with classical zeroth-order oracles (O(n) queries per round)
unmapped: Classical zeroth-order oracle queried 2n times per round (more than 'a few' points; finite-difference gradient)
Completely adaptive adversary: f_t chosen after observing x_t
settings.definition_quote: A classical zeroth-order oracle $O_f$ to the loss function $f$, queried with a vector $x\in\mathcal{K}$, outputs $O_f(x)=f(x)$.

symbols.rho_q: failure probability of quantum gradient estimation per round
symbols.p_q: failure probability of smoothness sub-module per round

conditions: losses convex and G-Lipschitz on K
K convex with diameter at most D
tuning: r'_t = rho^2 p/(8 pi sqrt(t n^9)(n+rho))

source.label: TQ
source.quote: Algorithm \ref{QOCO} with parameters $\eta_t=\frac{D}{G\sqrt{t}}, r_t=\frac{1}{\sqrt{tn}}, r^{\prime}_t=\frac{\rho^2 p}{8 \pi \sqrt{tn^9} (n +\rho)}$, can achieve the regret bound $O(DG\sqrt{T})$, with probability greater than $1-T(\rho+p)$, and its query complexity is $O(1)$ in each round.

results.notes: Holds with probability > 1 - T(rho+p). Proof's explicit bound is 3DG sqrt(T) + 2G sqrt(T), summarized as O(DG sqrt T). Uses 4 quantum oracle queries per round. Lemma 3 drops a (1+(2r')^n) factor approximately.

conditions: losses alpha-strongly convex and G-Lipschitz on K
K convex with diameter at most D
tuning: r_t = G^2/(t(2G sqrt(n) + alpha n D))
r'_t = G^2 rho^2 p/(8 pi t n^4 (n+rho)(2G sqrt(n)+alpha n D))

source.label: TAQ
source.quote: For $\alpha$-strongly convex loss functions, Algorithm \ref{QOCO} with parameters $\eta_t=\frac{1}{\alpha t}, r_t=\frac{G^2}{t(2G\sqrt{n}+\alpha nD)}, r^{\prime}_t=\frac{G^2\rho^2 p}{8 \pi tn^4 (n +\rho)(2G\sqrt{n}+\alpha nD)}$, can achieve the regret bound $O(G^2\log{T})$, with probability greater than $1-T(\rho+p)$, and its query complexity is $O(1)$ in each round.

results.notes: Proof gives (2G^2/alpha) log T + (3/2) G^2 log T; the stated O(G^2 log T) hides 1/alpha dependence. Probability > 1 - T(rho+p).

conditions: losses convex and G-Lipschitz on K
K convex with diameter at most D

source.label: TC
source.quote: Algorithm \ref{COCO} with parameters $\eta_t=\frac{D}{G\sqrt{t}}, r_t=\frac{1}{\sqrt{tn}}, r^{\prime}_t=\frac{\delta}{T\sqrt{tn^3}}$ can achieve the regret bound $O(DG\sqrt{T})$, with probability greater than $1-\delta$, and its query complexity is $O(n)$ in each round.

results.notes: Uses 2n classical zeroth-order queries per round (finite differences); feedback mapped to two_point loosely. Holds w.p. > 1-delta.
